text:
For two periods the Devils did most of the playing and spent most of the afternoon behind. Then Jack Hughes broke in alone early in the third, and New Jersey turned a 3-2 deficit into a 5-3 win over Calgary, its third straight.

The first period went the way Mike Fink of The Hockey News described it at the intermission: the Devils outshot the Flames 15-7, out-chanced them 1.88 expected goals to 0.53, and trailed 1-0, because Joel Hanley scored on a shot our model gave less than a 1% chance. New Jersey answered twice in 12 seconds early in the second, Luke Hughes and then Timo Meier, but Calgary hit back with Matt Coronato's 16% chance and a late Zach Whitecloud snap shot (3%). With Connor Hellebuyck getting the day off ahead of Saturday's game against the Jets, Jake Allen had allowed three on 21 shots, and the Flames' win chance stood at 71%.

Hughes's breakaway at 7:35 of the third tied it, a play Fink called his first game-changer in a while. Connor Brown won it at 16:02 with a 16% wrist shot that moved New Jersey from 52% to 90%; Devin Cooley had robbed him earlier in the period on a 33% look, the best chance of the game that didn't go in. Luke Hughes added the empty-net goal at 19:49. Jack Hughes finished with a goal and three assists, Meier a goal and an assist, and Daily Faceoff noted on Friday that Meier is now Switzerland's all-time leading NHL goal-scorer.

Over the full game the Devils earned this one: 3.88 expected goals to 2.33, 72 shot attempts to 55, and 74% of replays of every shot go their way. They did it without Brenden Dillon, who began a four-game suspension today, and they turn around tomorrow against Winnipeg. Calgary, which snapped a winless run in Pittsburgh on Wednesday, was outplayed for long stretches by a team that kept coming.
headline: Jack Hughes's breakaway flips it for the Devils
